source_review.notes: Reviewed the primary persistence paper by Driscoll et al., Okasaki's thesis and functional red-black paper, Bagwell's HAMT paper, and maintained/current Rust im, Clojure, Clojure PersistentVector, and Scala immutable-collection materials. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked version roots, reachable node sets, logical occurrence versus physical union counts, update footprint, height, version DAG, and transient token terminology.
Checked persistence level, logical/content/version/entry/node identity, root/reader/cache retention, and durable object IDs remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Partial, full, confluent, and retroactive models are not conflated.

evidence: Recomputed seven roots including empty and logical sizes 1+2+3+4+3+4=17.
Recomputed path-copy allocations 1+2+2+3+3+2=13 unique nodes.
Recomputed four multiply referenced objects: the v2/v3 node 2, v3/v4 node 6, and v4/v6 left nodes 2 and 1.
Recomputed v4 keys 1,2,4,6; v5 keys 2,3,4; and old/new values six/SIX at key 6.
Checked perfect-tree exercise copied-node counts for insert, replace, and delete.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Object counts are exact for the finite tuple implementation and are not allocator-byte estimates.

evidence: Verified old-version correctness from nonmutation/lifetime and new-version correctness inductively from copied ancestors and one changed child.
Verified point update work/allocation O(h), conditionally logarithmic only under a balance/height guarantee.
Verified deletion/rotation/augmentation copies the full changed frontier and recomputes metadata.
Verified physical live nodes are the union reachable from all roots/readers/caches, not sum of version sizes.
Verified root publication last gives strong in-memory failure isolation but not disk crash durability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Node-count asymptotics and page/byte amplification are reviewed separately.

evidence: Reviewed empty, duplicate/no-op, root/leaf/one/two-child deletion, rotations, sorted/reverse imbalance, branches from all versions, equal-content versions, and mutable values.

Reviewed refcount roots/overflow/cycles/deep destruction, GC pauses, epochs/stalled readers, arena dependency retention, iterator/caches, transient token misuse/freeze/failure, and writer CAS retries/ABA.

Reviewed hostile version creation/pinning, deep trees, expensive comparators/values, graph cycles/IDs/hashes, crash child-before-root ordering, schema/comparator migration, GC roots, and authorization/history leakage.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Quotas cover roots, updates, depth, live/retained bytes, reader age, diff/output, history, and transient duration.

evidence: The executable validates strict BST bounds in every version and exact in-order key sets.
It checks old-value preservation, branch isolation, untouched-left-subtree identity, logical occurrences, unique objects, and shared-object counts.
The proposed global validator distinguishes logical ADT correctness from implementation-specific maximal-sharing promises.
invariant_checking.notes: The trace covers insertion/value replacement in an unbalanced immutable tuple BST, not deletion, balancing, reclamation, concurrency, transients, or disk.

evidence: Reviewed persistence models, exact path reconstruction, complexity/retention/locality, deletion/balancing/augmentation, identity/iterators, and diff shortcuts.
Reviewed tracing/refcount/epoch/arena/ownership reclamation, failure semantics, transient builders, concurrent root publication/writer conflict/ABA, and value lifetime.
Reviewed logical/graph/content-addressed serialization, durable ordering/recovery/GC/migration, security/resource controls, branching references, faults, concurrency, and benchmarks.
proof_review.notes: In-memory immutability and durable storage persistence are explicitly separate properties.

evidence: Old/new version inductive proofs, complexity, memory reachability, publication, and disk durability are separately scoped.
Classical theory and current library behaviors are attached to named sources.
The finite tuple trace is explicitly not reclamation/concurrency/storage/performance proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No persistence technique or memory manager is claimed universally superior.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact fourteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded Python toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_path_copying_version_trace and reproduces versions, branching, value isolation, identity sharing, counts, and BST validity.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No balanced/delete/rotation behavior, allocation failure, refcount/GC/epoch/arena, transient, concurrent CAS, serialization, crash recovery, hostile parser, or production memory/tail behavior was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Progresses from persistence/version semantics through path reconstruction, complexity and branching, balancing/identity, reclamation, transients, concurrency, serialization/durability, security, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed immutable value ownership, stable handles/generations, old-reader retention telemetry, allocator/cache amplification, deletion/rotation metadata, root registries, refcount/GC/epoch/arena choices, transient batches, CAS conflicts/retries, content-addressed/version DAG formats, child-before-root durability, GC/quotas, migrations, and failure cleanup.

pedagogical_review.notes: Introduces Level II with formal persistence levels and reachability accounting, includes a fully reproduced branching/share trace, ten examples, and five progressive graduate exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Driscoll/Sarnak/Sleator/Tarjan, Okasaki, Bagwell, Rust im, Clojure, Scala, security, performance, reliability, operations, storage, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither arbitrary persistent ADTs, balanced deletion/rotation/augmentation, mutable-value isolation, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, refcount/GC/epoch/arena correctness, transient exclusivity, thread safety/linearizability/ABA/reclamation, durable serialization/crash recovery/GC, hostile-version/parser security, production memory/cache/GC/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
